title: Distinguish spinner affordance and deferred-action model for buttons
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Multiple teams have reported inconsistent behavior and visual affordance for 'loading' button states across themes and when icon-only buttons are used. Some variants show full opacity transitions and spinner overlays that obscure labels; others remove hover affordance and introduce click queueing without feedback. This ticket unifies how we present transient states for primary/secondary/ghost/icon buttons and defines a deferred-action model for long-running clicks (>= 800ms) to reduce accidental double-activations.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document a single spinner affordance pattern that works across light/dark and high-contrast themes and for both icon-only and label buttons.
Implement token updates for spinner size, offset, and backdrop opacity; tokens must be semantically named (e.g., token.button.loading.backdrop-opacity) and included in token migration guide.
Design spec includes visual examples for: primary, secondary, ghost, danger, and icon-only variants in normal, hovered, focused, disabled, and loading states.

Accessibility: spinner must be announced to screen readers (aria-live region pattern) and buttons in loading state should expose aria-busy=true. Keyboard focus states must remain visible during loading.

Deferred-action model: clicking a button that runs >800ms shows inline spinner and a cancellable state for the first 2s; after 2s the action becomes non-cancellable and button shows final busy state. Spec written and approved by PM/Eng.
Design tokens and CSS variables are backward-compatible; fallbacks provided for consumers that haven't migrated yet.
Design handoff includes Storybook stories and a small interaction prototype. Engineering PR references this ticket and passes QA checklist.
No visual regressions in baseline regression suite for button components across supported browsers.
Doc: Add entry to 'Button migration' page and update change log with examples and token mapping table.
technical_notes: Spinner overlay should prefer composited layers; avoid layout shifts by reserving width for label+spinner in layout token calculations.
For icon-only buttons, use a smaller spinner size that respects hitbox and visual balance; token: button.icon.loading.size = 12px on 40px hitbox.

Deferred-action timeline: 0-200ms: optimistic micro-animate; 200-800ms: show inline spinner; 800-2000ms: show cancellable overlay with 'Cancel' affordance; >2000ms: full busy state with disabled click and aria-busy.
Edge: On network retry scenarios, spinner re-enters cancellable window only if backend reports lengthened processing; otherwise show persistent busy state to prevent confusion.
Performance: avoid re-creating spinner DOM on every render; use a stable hidden element toggled by classes and rely on CSS animations.
Tokens: introduce semantic tokens — button.loading.backdrop, button.loading.spinnerSize, button.loading.gap, button.loading.transitionMs. Map to existing core tokens in migration doc.
Testing: Add automated visual regression snapshots for 6 themes × 5 variants × 3 states (normal/loading/disabled).
Coordination: ENG must add telemetry event for 'button_load_start' and 'button_load_cancel' to evaluate real-world cancel rates.
Fallback: For browsers without CSS variables, provide static classes using the closest fallback tokens.
qa_checklist: Cross-theme visual check in Storybook for all variants
Keyboard navigation preserves focus ring during loading
Screen reader announces loading state and cancel affordance
No layout shift when spinner appears
